proposed.text: An architect is designing a grab bar for the side wall of an accessible WC cubicle. The WC seat height is 450 mm AFF. At what height above finished floor should the horizontal grab bar be mounted?

options.text: 900 mm AFF — matching the lever handle and handrail height standard
300 mm AFF — as stated in the BP 344 grab bar specification
750 mm AFF — 300 mm above the 450 mm WC seat height
760 mm AFF — 300 mm above a 460 mm WC seat height

proposed.rationale: Correct answer: C — 750 mm AFF. The WC seat is 450 mm AFF and the grab bar sits 300 mm above the seat top, so 450 + 300 = 750 mm AFF. Source verbatim: 'The height of toilet seat shall be 450 mm.' (BP 344 2024 Revised IRR, PDF p.37 line 1199) and 'Both grab bars shall be installed 300 mm high from the top of the toilet seat to the top of the grab bars.' (PDF p.36 lines 1153-1154). Option D uses the erroneous 460 mm seat height, which is not in the source.
proposed.explanation: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR sets the WC seat height at 450 mm AFF (Appendix A, PDF p.37 line 1199) and requires both the fixed L-type and flip-up grab bars to be installed 300 mm above the top of the toilet seat (PDF p.36 lines 1153-1154). Therefore the grab bar AFF height = 450 + 300 = 750 mm. The 460 mm / 760 mm figures are not in the source and are the documented errors being corrected. The most common trap is reading '300 mm' as the absolute AFF height rather than as the offset above the seat.
